days.title: Timetable
days.description:
A timetable is a set of days that share the same prices. Most plans need only one, covering every day.

If weekends or public holidays are priced differently, name this one for the days it does cover. You can add another timetable at the end, and it stays part of this same plan.

The name you give it is put in front of every rate you enter next, so a weekend peak and a weekday peak can both exist.

data_description.same_every_day: Leave on unless weekends, weekdays or public holidays are priced differently.
data_description.days: Ignored while 'Every day is the same' is on. Public holidays need a holiday sensor, which is set under Configure.
data_description.name: Every day, Weekday, Weekend, Public holidays - whatever fits. It prefixes this timetable's rates.

allowance_counting.title: Allowance counting
allowance_counting.description:
Some plans give a period free or cheap only up to a daily cap. Your plan already says what the cap is and what you pay past it, and publishes both, whatever you choose here.

This only decides whether this integration keeps its own running total, so the price sensor switches to the fallback once the cap is spent. That keeps the Energy dashboard honest on these plans.

It is an estimate. It counts the meter you nominate and resets at local midnight. Your retailer meters and resets on their own terms, so it will not match your bill exactly and is not meant to.

Capped rates in this plan: {capped}

data.count_allowance: Count my usage against the cap

data_description.count_allowance: Off by default. With it off the price sensor reports the scheduled rate and says that the cap is not being accounted for.
data_description.import_energy_sensor: A total grid import energy sensor in kWh. Nothing is counted without one.

data_description.timetable: Rates are identified by their timetable and their name together, so a weekday Peak and a weekend Peak can both be called Peak at different prices. The rate is published as 'weekday.peak'. A rate from an older plan carries no timetable and keeps the name it already has.
data_description.information_constraints: Useful facts about this rate that other systems can look at. Pick from the list, or type your own and press enter. Each one becomes a switch-like sensor your automations can trigger on.
data_description.enforceable_constraints: Rules you are declaring to be part of what this rate means, so another system should treat them as a rule rather than a hint. This integration still enforces nothing — it only says so, and the consuming system decides what to do. A rule belongs in one list or the other, not both.
data_description.coasting_permitted: Tells other systems that letting a room drift is acceptable during this rate.
data_description.demand_period: A marker only. The monthly demand charge is not calculated here.
data_description.daily_allowance_kwh: Zero for none. Some plans give a period free only up to a daily cap.
data_description.fallback_rate: Only used when there is an allowance: what the energy costs once it is spent.

day_patterns_menu.title: Day patterns
day_patterns_menu.description:
A day pattern is a group of days that share the same timetable — every day, or weekdays and weekends separately, or a summer and a winter version.

Most plans need only one.

```
{plan}
```

data.name: Name
data.export_same_all_day: Feed-in is one price all day

data_description.same_every_day: Leave this on unless weekends, weekdays or public holidays are priced differently.
data_description.days: Ignored while 'Every day is the same' is on. Public holidays only appear as a choice once you nominate a holiday sensor under the general settings.
data_description.season_from: Optional. Leave both empty for all year. A range may cross the new year, for example 11-01 to 03-31.
data_description.season_to: Optional. Leave both empty for all year.
data_description.export_same_all_day: Turn off if the feed-in price changes through the day on this timetable, then set the feed-in rates and their times under Feed-in.
data_description.export_flat_cents: Used only while the switch above is on.

day_pattern_duplicate.title: Duplicate a day pattern
day_pattern_duplicate.description: Copies the time periods, so a weekend or a season can be built from a shape that already works.

periods_menu.description:

{plan}

period_add.title: Time period
period_add.description:
The start time is included and the end time is not, so one period can end at 16:00 and the next begin at 16:00. A period that runs to midnight ends at 00:00.

```
{plan}
```

data_description.prices_include_gst: Australian bills quote prices with GST included. Most European and US rate sheets quote them without.
data_description.valid_from: Optional. Leave empty unless you are recording a plan that started on a known date.
data_description.valid_to: Optional. When your retailer reprices, set this and add a new channel for the new plan, so past costs stay correct against the price that was actually in force.
data_description.holiday_sensor: Optional. A Workday sensor from Home Assistant's built-in Workday integration, which is off on a public holiday. Needed only if holidays are priced differently.
data_description.demand_rate_per_kw_month: Zero if you do not have one. Charged on your highest half-hour of demand in the month. The monthly amount is not calculated here.
data_description.monthly_charge: A subscription or plan fee charged once a month. Zero if you do not have one.
